review_status: Evidence reviewed 2026-11-17. North Pacific marine survey models and archival tagging support species-specific thermal habitat; configured SST intervals are warmer than the modeled preferred range, and bathymetry is only a weak proxy for pelagic salmon.

profile.size: Min limit 20-24 inches TL / Bag limit 1-2 per harvester / day
profile.diet: Small fish, crustaceans, squids, and pelagic prey
profile.behavior: Navigates West Coast kelp forests, rocky reefs, and coastal upwelling zones.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside preferred Pacific temperature range for chinook salmon.
factors.value_notes: Langan et al. (2024) modeled Chinook marine preferred SST at 3.6-12.3 °C (80% HDI), core 5.8-10.3 °C, median 8.3 °C and modal 8.7 °C from North Pacific survey data (1953-2022). Hinke et al. archival tags off Oregon/California independently found persistent use of 8-12 °C water. This supports SST as a strong marine habitat factor, but the configured 8-16 °C range and 10-14 °C ideal are shifted warmer and miss much of the modeled preferred interval. Results are North Pacific marine-phase models, not a stock-specific coastal catch curve.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, within prime Pacific depth zone for chinook salmon.
factors.value_notes: Chinook tagging documents fish vertical occupancy from the surface to hundreds of metres and seasonal changes in water-column depth. The runtime variable is seafloor bathymetry, not fish vertical depth; nearshore shelf association does not establish a universal 0-100 m bottom-depth preference. Retain bathymetry only as a weak shelf/offshore context proxy.

text.day: Full daylight when Pacific gamefish actively hunt.

timing.note: West Coast captain reports and biological upwelling patterns.
